findings.scope_note: SECONDARY LYMPHEDEMA ONLY (BCRL). Not applicable to primary lymphedema. Retained for completeness of evidence record — the RCT design and negative result may inform evidence standards across the field.
findings.title: ADRC + Lipotransfer Ineffective for BCRL: High-Quality Negative RCT
findings.summary: A double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase II RCT (n=80) found no clinical benefit of autologous adipose-derived regenerative cells (ADRCs) combined with lipotransfer vs. placebo for breast cancer-related lymphedema at 1 year. The primary outcome (limb volume change) and all objective secondary outcomes were negative. Both groups showed subjective improvement, consistent with placebo effect.
findings.clinical_implications: ADRC+lipotransfer should not be recommended for BCRL. This finding overrides prior positive observational and non-randomized studies. The placebo response in subjective outcomes reinforces the need for controlled trials in this field.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: Jørgensen 2024 PRS double-blind RCT (n=80, 1-year follow-up) is the primary evidence. Pre-RCT, observational data had suggested possible benefit. RCT clearly refutes this. High decision value: prunes ADRC+lipotransfer from future investigation unless substantially different protocols are proposed.

findings.title: Lymfactin (VEGF-C Gene Therapy) Phase II: Primary Endpoints Missed, Secondary Biomarker Signal
findings.summary: The Lymfactin Phase II RCT (n=39, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled) evaluated adenoviral VEGF-C gene therapy co-administered with VLNT surgery for BCRL. Primary endpoints (edema volume, QoL, lymphoscintigraphy at 12 months) showed no statistically significant difference between Lymfactin and placebo. A secondary endpoint — tissue dielectric constant (TDC) ratio, a device measure of skin interstitial fluid — favoured Lymfactin (P=0.020). Importantly, both arms improved vs baseline, providing the first controlled evidence that VLNT itself produces meaningful improvement.
findings.clinical_implications: Lymfactin's additive benefit over VLNT surgery alone is not established by primary endpoints. The TDC secondary signal is hypothesis-generating. The trial is underpowered (n=39) and 12 months may be insufficient for lymphangiogenesis maturation. VLNT's independent efficacy is strengthened by its effect in the placebo arm of a controlled trial.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: Rannikko 2025 PRS Phase II RCT. Primary endpoints missed. Secondary biomarker (TDC ratio) significant at P=0.020. Small n (39). The trial establishes VLNT efficacy in controlled setting — a secondary finding of considerable independent value. Lymfactin's drug effect unproven. Lymfactin Phase I (Pajula 2025 JPRAS) also published; 12 patients, 4-year follow-up; 6/12 reduced/discontinued compression; positive QoL but uncontrolled.

findings.title: VLNT Shows Positive Effect in First Controlled Multicenter Setting
findings.summary: A secondary finding from the Lymfactin Phase II RCT is that vascularized lymph node transfer (VLNT) surgery produced objective improvement vs baseline in both trial arms (active drug and placebo). This is notable because prior evidence for VLNT has been almost entirely single-arm retrospective. This controlled setting strengthens, but does not fully validate, VLNT's efficacy.
findings.clinical_implications: VLNT's evidence base is slightly stronger than most other surgical lymphedema interventions. However, the trial was not designed to test VLNT efficacy independently, and selection/surgical criteria differences preclude broad generalization. The lack of a surgery-naive control arm means we still cannot rule out natural history as a confound.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: derived from placebo arm improvement in Lymfactin Phase II RCT. Still single-site (Turku/Nordic centers). Surgical evidence gap in this field remains significant. All LVA/VLNT studies outside this trial are single-arm or retrospective.

findings.scope_note: SECONDARY LYMPHEDEMA ONLY (filarial). Not applicable to primary lymphedema. Retained for completeness.
findings.title: Doxycycline for Filarial Lymphedema: Reduces Acute Attacks, Unclear Limb Improvement at 24 Months
findings.summary: A double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT in Tanzania (n=362, LF lymphedema stages 1-3) found that doxycycline (200mg or 100mg/day x 42 days) did NOT improve limb condition at 24 months vs placebo; the placebo group paradoxically showed the highest limb improvement rate (23.4% vs 14.4-15.2%). However, doxycycline significantly reduced acute ADL (adenolymphangitis) attacks in the first 6 months. Doxycycline 100mg was associated with halting of disease progression (OR 0.53). Hygiene was the dominant factor preventing acute attacks overall.
findings.clinical_implications: For filarial lymphedema, doxycycline's primary value may be in reducing cellulitis/acute attack frequency rather than reversing established lymphedema. Hygiene instruction remains the most evidence-supported intervention for filarial lymphedema.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: Ngenya 2024 AJTMH RCT (n=362, Tanzania, 2-year follow-up). Nuanced result: acute attack prevention clear, limb improvement at 24 months negative on primary endpoint.

findings.title: Chamomile and Olive Oils as CDT Adjunct: No Benefit vs CDT Alone
findings.summary: A double-blind RCT (n=63, BCRL) found no statistically significant difference in lymphedema volume, range of motion, or QoL between CDT alone, CDT+olive oil, and CDT+chamomile/olive oil combination. All groups improved, consistent with CDT's known efficacy. Chamomile and olive oil massage was safe.
findings.clinical_implications: Chamomile and olive oils, when added to CDT, provide no additional measurable clinical benefit over standard CDT. The interventions are safe but do not warrant clinical recommendation beyond standard CDT for BCRL.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: Sheikhi 2024 LRB double-blind RCT (n=63). All groups used CDT; differences between groups not significant. Small n and relatively short follow-up.

findings.title: Self-Administered CDT Non-Inferior to Therapist-Administered CDT at 3 Months
findings.summary: A non-inferiority RCT (n=50, BCRL) found self-administered CDT (SELF group, n=25) was not inferior to certified lymphedema therapist-administered CDT (CLT group, n=25) on lymphedema severity and health-related outcomes at end-of-treatment and 3-month follow-up. Both groups showed significant improvement during CDT.
findings.clinical_implications: Self-administered CDT may be a viable maintenance approach for patients with BCRL, potentially reducing the frequency of specialist visits needed. Limitations: small n (50 total), 3-month follow-up only, single-center, all participants received initial training.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: Gultekin 2025 BCRT non-inferiority RCT (n=50, 3-month f/u). Short follow-up is the key limitation.

findings.scope_note: SECONDARY LYMPHEDEMA ONLY (BCRL prevention). Not applicable to primary lymphedema. Retained as strong evidence for surgical prevention principles that are conceptually relevant to the field.
findings.title: ILR/LYMPHA Reduces BCRL Incidence by ~64-75%: Accumulating Prevention Evidence
findings.summary: Multiple meta-analyses and large case series of immediate lymphatic reconstruction (ILR/LYMPHA) at time of ALND consistently show BCRL incidence reductions of 64-75% vs. ALND without ILR. In one 13-year series: 14.6% lymphedema rate with LYMPHA vs ~40% without. The evidence base, while predominantly observational/comparative-cohort, is large and consistent.
findings.clinical_implications: ILR/LYMPHA should be offered to patients undergoing level III ALND at centers with microsurgical capability. Lacks a major powered RCT, but the magnitude and consistency of benefit across centers supports adoption.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: Multiple systematic reviews and meta-analyses in database. No RCT yet for ILR/LYMPHA vs. control, but MSK trial NCT06144164 (n=285, Phase 3) is actively recruiting.

findings.title: Topical Tacrolimus: Pilot Signal in BCRL, Phase II/III RCT Enrolling
findings.summary: An open-label, single-arm Phase II pilot trial (n=18, BCRL stage I-II, 6-month treatment) found topical tacrolimus 0.1% significantly reduced arm volume (mean -130 mL, -3.6%) and L-Dex. QoL improved. Lymph flow showed modest positive trends but was inconclusive. The TACLE trial (NCT06306274, n=80, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 12 months) is now recruiting to test these findings in a controlled setting.
findings.clinical_implications: Topical tacrolimus is not established as standard treatment for BCRL. The pilot is uncontrolled and the volume reduction (3.6%) is small. The TACLE RCT, if positive, would represent the first approved topical pharmacotherapy for lymphedema.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: Uncontrolled pilot (n=18); TACLE protocol published April 2025. TACLE results expected 2026-2027.

findings.title: PIEZO1 Mechanosensory Pathway: Preclinical Target for Lymphatic Drug Development
findings.summary: PIEZO1, a mechanosensitive ion channel, is a critical regulator of lymphatic development and valve formation. Loss-of-function PIEZO1 variants cause autosomal-recessive primary lymphedema (lymphatic malformation type 6), including presentations with neonatal hydrops, chylothorax, and multi-region lymphedema. Sabine et al. (Journal of Clinical Investigation, May 2024) provide direct mechanistic data: in lymphatic endothelial cells, PIEZO1 activation triggers exocytosis of ANGPT2 and ectodomain shedding of TIE1, placing PIEZO1 upstream of the ANGPT2/TIE/FOXO1 signaling axis already implicated in primary lymphedema genetics. In preclinical mouse models, the PIEZO1 agonist Yoda1 suppressed post-surgical lymphedema. A separate case report (2023) documents persistent chylothorax as a presenting feature of biallelic PIEZO1 variants, extending the recognized phenotypic spectrum.
findings.clinical_implications: This is now one of the better-mechanistically-supported pathways in primary lymphedema genetics: human genetic association (PIEZO1 variants cause disease), a defined molecular mechanism (PIEZO1->ANGPT2->TIE1/FOXO1), and a preclinical pharmacologic proof-of-concept (Yoda1 in mice). It is not a treatment — Yoda1 has not been tested in humans, and mouse post-surgical lymphedema models have a poor track record of translating to human primary lymphedema (see preclinical translation caveat used throughout this KB). The chylothorax case report is a reminder that PIEZO1-related disease can present outside the limbs and should prompt genetic testing in atypical presentations.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: Multiple PIEZO1 papers in database, most not lymphedema-relevant. Key lymphedema-relevant paper: JCI 2024. Yoda1 agonist preclinical only.

W31 2026 deep synthesis: This finding has carried an empty supporting_papers list since 2026-04-12 despite describing a specific mechanism (PIEZO1->ANGPT2->TIE/FOXO1) verbatim — traced the claim to its source paper (Sabine et al., JCI 2024) and added it, plus a 2023 case report extending the phenotype to isolated chylothorax. Confidence raised from 'low' to 'low_to_moderate': the mechanism is now backed by an identifiable, well-designed mechanistic study rather than an uncited claim, though it remains preclinical/mouse-model evidence for the therapeutic angle specifically.

W32 2026 deep synthesis: Added two more preclinical mechanistic papers. (1) EPHB4-RASA1 Inhibition of PIEZO1 Ras Activation Drives Lymphatic Valvulogenesis (Circulation Research, 2024) shows EPHB4/RASA1 act upstream of PIEZO1-Ras signaling specifically in lymphatic valve development, in mouse knockin/knockout models plus human dermal lymphatic endothelial cells in vitro -- extends the PIEZO1 mechanistic map from a single ANGPT2/TIE1/FOXO1 axis to a broader valvulogenesis node. (2) A conference abstract reports a Piezo2-Vegfr3-Prox1 signaling axis regulating adipose-tissue lymphangiogenesis in mouse single-cell RNA-seq data, connecting PIEZO-family mechanosensing to obesity-associated lymphatic dysfunction. Confidence unchanged at low_to_moderate -- both are preclinical/mouse or in-vitro mechanistic work, not therapeutic or human translational evidence. Broadens rather than strengthens the evidence tier.

findings.scope_note: SECONDARY LYMPHEDEMA ONLY (BCRL prevention via surgical de-escalation in breast cancer). Retained as the highest-quality lymphedema prevention RCT in the database.
findings.title: INSEMA: Omission of Axillary Surgery Reduces Lymphedema Risk Without Compromising Survival
findings.summary: The INSEMA trial (n=4,858, NEJM 2025) demonstrated that omission of axillary surgery vs. sentinel-node biopsy in cN0 breast cancer is non-inferior for 5-year invasive disease-free survival (91.9% vs 91.7%). The surgery-omission group had a lower incidence of lymphedema. A small increase in axillary recurrence (1.0% vs 0.3%) was observed, but mortality was lower in the surgery-omission group.
findings.clinical_implications: For selected cN0 breast cancer patients (predominantly T1), omission of sentinel-node biopsy is oncologically non-inferior and reduces lymphedema burden. Patients and surgeons should be aware of axillary recurrence trade-off.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: NEJM 2025 INSEMA trial. Large n, Phase III, non-inferiority design.

findings.scope_note: SECONDARY LYMPHEDEMA FOCUS (BCRL). L-Dex is also used in primary lymphedema monitoring; partially cross-applicable.
findings.title: Bioimpedance Spectroscopy (L-Dex) for Subclinical BCRL Detection: Validated Utility
findings.summary: L-Dex (bioimpedance spectroscopy) has accumulated evidence as a reliable method for detecting subclinical BCRL before clinical signs appear. Growing adoption in oncology centers for post-ALND surveillance to trigger early CDT intervention.
findings.clinical_implications: L-Dex provides an objective, quantitative measure for early BCRL detection at a subclinical stage when CDT intervention is most effective. L-Dex is a surrogate biomarker — it does not directly measure lymphatic function.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: Multiple bioimpedance papers in database. L-Dex threshold variability across studies remains a limitation.

findings.title: Global Evidence Gap: LVA and VLNT Lack RCT Evidence
findings.summary: The vast majority of LVA (lymphaticovenular anastomosis) and VLNT (vascularized lymph node transfer) evidence comes from single-arm retrospective case series or prospective cohorts without control arms. No published RCT has randomized patients between surgical and non-surgical management for established lymphedema. Volume reduction outcomes vary widely across series, complicated by heterogeneous patient selection, staging criteria, surgical techniques, and lack of standardized outcome measures.
findings.clinical_implications: Clinical adoption of LVA/VLNT has outpaced the evidence base. Centers report widely varying outcomes. Patients considering surgery should understand this evidence gap. Surgical outcomes are highly dependent on disease stage (ISL Stage I-IIa performs better), ICG pattern, and center experience.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: Review of 461 papers confirms this is a persistent field-wide limitation. The single exception is the Lymfactin Phase II trial which included VLNT in both arms.

W19 2026 deep synthesis: Two W19 items reinforce the persistent gap. (1) pm_42028378 (JPRAS Open) — bibliometric of 50 most-cited lymphatic surgery papers confirms case series dominance. (2) pm_42085896 (J Surg Res) — single-center retrospective of 51 LLL patients comparing VLNT recipient sites. No new RCT in primary scope.

W24 2026 deep synthesis: gap reinforced. pm_42208734 (JVS-VL) PEER umbrella SR synthesizing 26 systematic reviews / 14 meta-analyses (2010-2025) for the forthcoming AVF/AVLS guidelines found NO RCTs for lymphatic microsurgery; conclusions rested on 4 moderate-quality treatment SRs + 1 high-quality prevention SR. pm_42001630 (JPRAS) retrospective LVA (n=123) vs VLNT (n=28), >=1y follow-up: LVA gives faster <3-month gains, VLNT improves more slowly through 12 months; still single-center retrospective, no randomization. No new RCT in primary scope.

W31 2026 deep synthesis: Added 2 more studies, both still within the established evidence-gap pattern: (1) a retrospective, single-arm study of LVA specifically in adult-onset primary lower-limb lymphedema (no control arm); (2) a retrospective University Hospital Zurich cohort (2016-2023) comparing LVA/VLNT outcomes between primary and secondary lymphedema patients — notable because it is one of the few surgical-outcomes studies with a defined comparator group by lymphedema etiology, but the comparator is etiology-based, not surgery-vs-no-surgery, so it does not close the RCT gap this finding tracks. Confidence remains high for the core claim (no RCT evidence exists comparing surgical to non-surgical management); primary-lymphedema-specific surgical case volume is slowly growing but the evidence tier is unchanged.

findings.title: FLT4 Variant Functional Characterization: VUS Reclassification Advancing in Milroy Disease
findings.summary: Two related publications (Filina et al., Current Issues in Molecular Biology, January 2026; and Monaghan et al., Clinical Genetics, December 2024) use in vitro kinase assays and clinical cohort screening (n=24 primary lymphedema patients) to reclassify FLT4 'variants of uncertain significance' (VUS) in Milroy disease. The c.3175G>C variant (p.A1059P) shows measurably decreased VEGFR3 kinase activity in vitro. Monaghan et al. additionally identify a novel likely-pathogenic variant (c.3028A>C) and support pathogenicity of c.3175G>C and c.3298T>C in their own cohort. A third paper (Ta-Shma/Krantz group style mechanistic study, Cardiovascular Research 2024) shows FLT4 variants causing Tetralogy of Fallot aggregate FLT4 protein differently in endothelial cells than Milroy-causing variants, offering a candidate mechanism for why FLT4 mutations produce non-overlapping cardiac vs. lymphatic phenotypes. A fourth report (Birth Defects Research 2023) describes two further novel FLT4 variants (p.Ser1275Thr, p.Ser1275Arg) in prenatally diagnosed hereditary lymphedema type 1.
findings.clinical_implications: The FLT4/VEGFR3 variant catalog for Milroy disease continues to grow steadily; functional (kinase activity) data remain the strongest available tool for reclassifying VUS, but only a minority of reported variants have been functionally tested. The TOF-vs-Milroy mechanistic divergence work is preclinical (transfected endothelial cells) and does not yet change genetic counseling — pleiotropy should still be assumed possible for any novel FLT4 variant until proven otherwise. None of these four papers report a therapeutic intervention; all are diagnostic/mechanistic.

evolution_log.note: W16 2026 deep synthesis: Filina 2026 (Curr Issues Mol Biol) — in vitro kinase assay showing c.3175G>C has decreased VEGFR3 kinase activity. Monaghan 2024 (Cardiovascular Research) — pleiotropic FLT4 mechanisms distinguish cardiac from lymphedema variants.

W31 2026 deep synthesis: Added 3 more papers to the FLT4 variant-catalog and mechanism literature: a companion functional paper (Monaghan et al. 2024) that was previously described narratively but not linked in supporting_papers, 2 more novel variants from a small prenatal case series (n=2), and a cell-based mechanistic paper on FLT4 pleiotropy (cardiac vs. lymphatic phenotype divergence). None of these change the confidence tier — still functional-VUS-reclassification-level evidence, not RCT or large-cohort replication. Confidence remains low_to_moderate.

findings.title: Erg/Fli1 ETS Transcription Factor Pair Required for Lymphatic Endothelial Integrity: Mouse Model Data
findings.summary: Yang et al. (Journal of Clinical Investigation, March 2026) used inducible lymphatic endothelial cell-specific deletion of ETS transcription factors Erg and Fli1 in adult mice to show that combined loss causes fatal lymphatic failure — including chylothorax, chylous ascites, and impaired lymphatic drainage. Single deletion of either factor alone was not lethal, indicating cooperative/redundant function.
findings.clinical_implications: Erg and Fli1 are not currently classified as primary lymphedema disease genes in humans, but their cooperative requirement for lymphatic valve gene programs and LEC identity places them in the same regulatory network as FOXC2, PROX1, and GATA2.

evolution_log.note: W16 2026 deep synthesis: Yang et al., JCI 2026. Mouse inducible deletion model. No human mutation data reported. Hypothesis-generating for potential novel disease genes.

findings.title: Novel Biallelic FAT4 Splicing Variant Expands Hennekam Syndrome 2 Allelic Spectrum
findings.summary: Mascarenhas & Gupta (American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A, April 2026) report a 15-month-old child with peripheral lymphedema, dysmorphic facies, and camptodactyly harboring a novel biallelic splicing variant c.12479+3A>G in FAT4. The variant expands the allelic spectrum of Hennekam lymphangiectasia-lymphedema syndrome 2 (FAT4-associated, OMIM 616006).
findings.clinical_implications: Adds to the growing variant catalog for FAT4-Hennekam 2 syndrome. A single case with a novel splice variant does not change diagnostic practice but is a useful curation datapoint. FAT4 should remain on comprehensive primary-lymphedema gene panels.

evolution_log.note: W16 2026 deep synthesis: Single case report published 2026-04-16. N=1. Splicing prediction supports likely-pathogenic classification but no in vitro confirmation reported.

findings.title: GJC2 and OBSCN Co-segregating Variants in Autosomal-Dominant Primary Lymphedema Pedigree
findings.summary: Shi et al. (Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, January 2026) report a four-generation Chinese pedigree with autosomal-dominant generalized primary lymphedema. WES + Sanger in 26 relatives identified two novel heterozygous missense variants co-segregating with disease: GJC2 c.287G>T (p.Gly96Val) and OBSCN c.22393T>A. Authors propose possible digenic or modifier contribution of OBSCN.
findings.clinical_implications: GJC2 (connexin 47) is an established primary lymphedema gene; a novel GJC2 missense variant in the transmembrane domain is mechanistically plausible. OBSCN co-segregation in one family is hypothesis-generating but not sufficient to add it to diagnostic gene panels. Do not counsel families on OBSCN as a lymphedema gene based on this report.

evolution_log.note: W16 2026 deep synthesis: Single-pedigree report. The GJC2 variant is the more credible causal contributor. OBSCN involvement is speculative. No replication in unrelated pedigrees.

findings.title: MR Thoracic Ductography Correlates With Clinical Stage in Primary Lower-Extremity Lymphedema (n=279)
findings.summary: Liu et al. (Vascular Medicine, February 2026) report MR thoracic ductography (MRTD) findings in 279 patients with primary lower-extremity lymphedema stratified by ISL stage (I/II/III). The study proposes imaging features of the central lymphatic system that correlate with clinical stage. This is one of the largest imaging cohorts limited to primary lymphedema published to date.
findings.clinical_implications: Suggests MRTD may have a role in pre-operative characterization of primary lymphedema beyond peripheral ICG lymphography. Not yet validated against treatment-outcome data. Imaging is a surrogate — correlation with clinical stage is expected and does not establish prognostic or treatment-predictive value.

evolution_log.note: W16 2026 deep synthesis: Liu 2026 Vasc Med. Cohort size (n=279) is unusually large for primary-lymphedema-only imaging. Cross-sectional design; no longitudinal outcomes.

W19 2026 deep synthesis: Sleboda et al. AJMG-A 2026 extends central-lymphatic-imaging signal into Noonan syndrome (RASopathy). Small (n=10 NS vs 10 controls), but controlled. The two cohorts together support central lymphatic imaging as a sensitive readout in primary lymphatic dysfunction.

findings.title: LPA → LPA4/LPA6 → Rho-Kinase → NF-κB → FOXC2 Axis Defines a Druggable Upstream Pathway for Lymphatic Valve Maintenance
findings.summary: Yasuda et al. (Journal of Clinical Investigation, January 2026) identified the GPCR pair LPA4 and LPA6 — receptors for the bioactive lipid lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) — as upstream regulators of FOXC2 expression and lymphatic valve formation. Lymphatic-endothelial-cell-specific deletion of Lpa4 and Lpa6 in mice phenocopies LEC-specific Foxc2 deletion. Pharmacologic inhibition of NF-κB or Rho-kinase impaired valve maintenance.
findings.clinical_implications: Mechanistic preclinical work only — does not change current care for lymphedema-distichiasis. The axis suggests testable hypotheses for future LDS-targeted therapeutics. None of this is clinically actionable today.

evolution_log.note: W18 2026 deep synthesis: Yasuda et al., JCI 2026-01-13 (PMID 41528806). LEC-specific Lpa4/Lpa6 conditional knockouts recapitulate FOXC2-deficient valve phenotype. No human translation steps reported.

findings.title: Million Veteran Program GWAS Identifies First Multi-Population Lymphedema and Lymphedema+CVI Loci
findings.summary: Peloso et al. (Circulation: Genomic and Precision Medicine, April 2026) report the first multi-population genome-wide association study dedicated to lymphedema and chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) using the Million Veteran Program. Cancer cases were excluded. Eleven genome-wide significant variants emerged: 8 for CVI-only, 1 for lymphedema-only, and 2 for lymphedema+CVI. Three CVI-only loci replicated in the UK Biobank.
findings.clinical_implications: Hypothesis-generating, not clinically actionable. Polygenic risk scoring is not yet recommended for primary-lymphedema risk stratification or counseling.

evolution_log.note: W18 2026 deep synthesis: Peloso et al., Circ Genom Precis Med, pub 2026-04-22 (PMID 42017216). First dedicated multi-population GWAS of lymphedema and CVI excluding cancer cases. Skepticism flag: lymphedema case ascertainment relies on EHR phecodes, which under-capture primary lymphedema.

findings.title: GLP-1 Agonists for Lymphedema: Biological Rationale, No Trial Results Yet
findings.summary: GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide) produce substantial weight loss (15-22%) and have anti-inflammatory properties. Given that obesity is a major driver of lymphedema severity, and GLP-1 receptors are expressed on immune cells, there is scientific rationale for exploring these agents in lymphedema. As of April 2026, no trial results specific to lymphedema have been published. Preclinical mechanistic support added W24 2026: GLP-1 receptors were found enriched specifically in lymphatic endothelial cells, and semaglutide increased the ex-vivo pumping capacity of isolated collecting lymphatics via NO-dependent vasodilation.
findings.clinical_implications: Cannot currently be recommended for lymphedema outside of their approved indications (obesity, T2DM). Results expected 2026-2027. The critical question is whether the benefit exceeds what would be predicted from weight loss alone.

evolution_log.note: Baseline synthesis: GLP-1 for lymphedema referenced in multiple reviews. No published trial results.

W24 2026 deep synthesis: pm_42231627 (Microcirculation) — scRNA-seq/confocal localized Glp1r to lymphatic endothelium; semaglutide raised collecting-lymphatic pumping ex vivo in WT, diet-induced-obese and ApoE-KO mice (NO-mediated). Provides a direct lymphatic-pumping mechanism beyond weight loss, but remains ex-vivo/animal data with no human or primary-lymphedema outcomes. Confidence stays LOW (preclinical; translation record in lymphatics is poor).

findings.title: KRAS-G12D Drives Lymphatic Valve Loss via MMP Upregulation: Druggable Mechanism in KRAS-Mutant Lymphatic Malformations
findings.summary: Bowles et al. (Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis, and Vascular Biology, 2026) used Flt4CreERT2;Kras-LSL-G12D;Prox1GFP mice and KRAS-G12D-expressing human dermal lymphatic endothelial cells to show lymphatic-restricted KRAS-G12D significantly attenuated valve development. KRAS-G12D LECs upregulated matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs); pharmacologic MMP inhibition rescued valve formation in 3D culture.
findings.clinical_implications: Identifies MMP inhibition as a candidate strategy in KRAS-mutant lymphatic anomalies. No MMP inhibitor is currently in human lymphatic-disease trials. Lymphedema preclinical translation has a poor track record.

evolution_log.note: W19 2026 deep synthesis: Bowles 2026 ATVB. Mouse cKO + 3D culture of human LECs. Mechanism plausible. Decision usefulness held to 4/10: no MMP inhibitor in human lymphatic-disease trials.

findings.title: RAS-MAPK Pathway Variants (LZTR1, MAP2K1, RAF1) Identified in Non-Syndromic Primary Lymphedema — First Report
findings.summary: Belanova et al. (Lymphology, August 2025; PMID 40803040) retrospectively analyzed 408 Italian primary lymphedema patients and identified five variants in LZTR1, MAP2K1, and RAF1 — four previously unreported — with in silico molecular modeling supporting potential pathogenicity for a RAF1 variant. Critically, the study patients did not carry a Noonan syndrome diagnosis; the variants appeared in clinically non-syndromic primary lymphedema. A PubMed search returns zero prior publications linking LZTR1 to lymphedema in any context. RAF1 and MAP2K1 in the lymphedema context have been reported exclusively in syndromic Noonan/RASopathy prior to this paper.
findings.clinical_implications: If replicated, this finding would blur the diagnostic boundary between syndromic RASopathy (Noonan syndrome + lymphedema) and non-syndromic primary lymphedema, suggesting germline RAS/MAPK pathway activation below the Noonan syndrome threshold can still disrupt lymphatic development. Immediate clinical implications are limited: no functional validation was performed, the Italian cohort may have population-specific effects, and independent replication is required before these genes are added to standard primary-lymphedema gene panels. Genetic counselors encountering primary lymphedema patients with LZTR1, MAP2K1, or RAF1 variants of uncertain significance may cite this paper as early-stage supporting evidence, but should not treat it as established.

evolution_log.note: W22 2026 deep synthesis: Belanova et al., Lymphology Aug 2025 (PMID 40803040). Italian cohort n=408, retrospective. 5 variants in LZTR1/MAP2K1/RAF1, 4 novel. Computational pathogenicity only — no functional assays. Zero PubMed hits for LZTR1+lymphedema. RAF1 and MAP2K1 in lymphedema context previously reported only in syndromic Noonan. Companion paper (same cohort): HGF-MET pathway (Kozáčiková 2025, PMID 40245437). Importance 6 / Evidence 4 / Novelty 7 / Decision 3 / Calibration 8.

findings.title: HGF-MET Signaling Pathway Variants in Primary Lymphedema: Italian Cohort Extends Prior Art
findings.summary: Kozáčiková et al. (Lymphology, April 2025; PMID 40245437) identified 8 variants in HGF, MET, and CBL genes in 408 Italian primary lymphedema patients — 7 previously unreported. Molecular modeling supported pathogenicity of 2 MET missense variants. HGF-MET is a recognized secondary-tier lymphedema pathway: HGF as a lymphangiogenesis factor was established in 2005 (Kajiya), HGF/MET mutations in primary lymphedema were first reported in 2008 (Finegold, PMID 18564920), and the same Italian group included MET/HGF in their 2018 NGS panel of 116 patients. The 2025 paper is the largest dedicated application of this pathway screen (n=408) and adds 7 novel variants, but does not establish a new pathway.
findings.clinical_implications: HGF-MET is on some existing comprehensive gene panels (20+ gene academic panels) but is behind VEGFR-3/FLT4, FOXC2, GATA2, and PROX1 in diagnostic yield. This study does not produce a practice-changing finding but contributes to the ongoing effort to resolve the ~64% of familial and ~92% of sporadic primary lymphedema cases without a molecular diagnosis. Variant yield (~2% of cohort had HGF/MET/CBL variants) is consistent with prior data from this group.

evolution_log.note: W22 2026 deep synthesis: Kozáčiková et al., Lymphology Apr 2025 (PMID 40245437). Italian cohort n=408. 8 variants in HGF/MET/CBL, 7 novel. Computational pathogenicity only. Extends prior art back to Finegold 2008 and Kajiya 2005. A 2025 review (PMID 40766782) already lists HGF/MET as established lymphedema axis. Companion paper (same cohort): Belanova 2025 RAS-MAPK. Importance 5 / Evidence 4 / Novelty 4 / Decision 3 / Calibration 9.

W31 2026 deep synthesis: Added an independent single-family HGF variant report (Int J Mol Sci, May 2024) that predates the 408-patient Italian cohort HGF/MET/CBL paper. Different cohort, same candidate gene (HGF), n=1 family. This is a second independent line of evidence nominating HGF as a lymphedema candidate gene, but a case report cannot move the confidence tier on its own — remains low. Note for future curation: this 2024 case report may be part of the prior literature the Italian cohort authors cite as rationale for including HGF/MET/CBL in their panel; treat as background, not independent replication of their specific variants.

findings.title: Subclinical Central Lymphatic Abnormalities Detected in Noonan Syndrome by MR-Lymphangiography (n=10 vs 10 controls)
findings.summary: Cross-sectional, controlled imaging study (American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A, 2026; ingested via 2026-05-09 scan) comparing 10 individuals with Noonan syndrome (4 with peripheral lymphedema, 6 without) to 10 age- and sex-matched cardiovascularly healthy controls using non-contrast T2 MR-lymphangiography, near-infrared fluorescence imaging, and strain-gauge plethysmography. 89% (8/9) of Noonan individuals showed thoracic-duct morphology variations vs 20% (2/10) of controls (p<0.05). Central lymphatic abnormalities were identified in 5/9 Noonan individuals — including 3 without overt clinical lymphatic disease. Abnormal peripheral collective vessel conduction (retrograde or absent flow) was observed only in Noonan individuals with overt lymphedema.
findings.clinical_implications: Suggests that central lymphatic involvement may be common in Noonan syndrome, including in patients without clinically apparent lymphedema. The finding raises the question of whether MR lymphangiography should be considered in selected Noonan patients. It does NOT yet justify population-wide screening. Primary care and cardiology counseling should still be driven by clinical signs.

evolution_log.note: W19 2026 deep synthesis: Sleboda et al. AJMG-A 2026. n=10 NS vs 10 matched controls; multimodal imaging; cross-sectional. Extends the central-lymphatic-imaging finding (Liu 2026 in non-syndromic primary lymphedema, n=279) into syndromic primary territory (RASopathy). Importance 6 / Evidence 5 / Novelty 7 / Decision 4 / Calibration 9.

findings.title: mTOR/MEK-Targeted Therapy for Neonatal Central & Generalized Lymphatic Anomalies: Efficacy Signal With a New Infant Dyslipidemia Safety Signal
findings.summary: Converging 2025-2026 reports describe targeted pharmacotherapy (mTOR inhibitor sirolimus, and/or MEK inhibitors) for severe neonatal/infant primary lymphatic anomalies — central conducting lymphatic anomaly (CCLA) and generalized lymphatic anomaly (GLA), including presentations with fetal hydrops. A CCLA case series (pm_40835771, n with pathogenic variants in 4) reported substantial clinical improvement, improved lymphatic flow on MR lymphangiography, and no relapse at mean 10.3 months after taper. A neonatal-GLA-with-hydrops report (pm_42216259) and a narrative synthesis (pm_42194698) point the same direction. However, a paired safety analysis (pm_42217144) found dyslipidemia is near-universal in sirolimus-treated infants (100% hypertriglyceridemia, 90% hypercholesterolemia in n=10) with a strong VigiBase disproportionality signal in infants (aROR 147).
findings.clinical_implications: Genotype-directed mTOR/MEK therapy is a promising option for otherwise life-threatening neonatal CCLA/GLA, but all efficacy evidence is case-series/anecdotal with short follow-up and no controls. The new safety data argue for routine lipid monitoring in infants started on sirolimus. Not generalizable to adult-onset primary lymphedema.

evolution_log.note: W24 2026 deep synthesis (new finding). Importance moderate-high for this rare severe population; evidence low (uncontrolled case series + retrospective cohort + disproportionality analysis). Efficacy and safety reports synthesized together to avoid one-sided optimism. Full text of pm_42216259 not retrievable (PubMed abstract unavailable).

W31 2026 deep synthesis: Added 3 more case-level reports: (1) a complex lymphatic anomaly (CLA) case in which sirolimus monotherapy lost effectiveness over time and trametinib (MEK inhibitor) was added with reported synergistic response — the first documented trametinib+sirolimus combination case in this line of evidence; (2) sirolimus monotherapy achieving full resolution of tongue lymphangioma circumscriptum over 17 months; (3) sirolimus for recurrent chylothorax/edema in an infant with Noonan syndrome (RASopathy-associated generalized lymphatic anomaly). All three are single case reports with no control arm and non-standardized outcome assessment. They reinforce an accumulating but still uncontrolled case-level signal for mTOR/MEK-targeted therapy across multiple lymphatic-anomaly subtypes and genetic backgrounds (isolated CLA, RASopathy-associated). Confidence tier unchanged (low_to_moderate) — case-report accumulation does not substitute for a comparative study, and the prior infant-dyslipidemia safety signal from this finding's evolution history still applies.

W32 2026 deep synthesis: Added a 2-case report of prenatal (in-utero, from 32-33 weeks gestation) plus postnatal sirolimus for extensive congenital capillary-lymphatic-venous malformations (CLVMs) with fetal complications (intralesional bleeding, polyhydramnios). Adds a prenatal-initiation data point to the case-level evidence base for mTOR-targeted therapy in severe congenital lymphatic anomalies. Still single-arm case-report evidence with no comparator; confidence tier unchanged at low_to_moderate.

findings.title: Primary Lymphedema May Reflect Endothelial Barrier/Permeability Defects Rather Than Fibrotic Obstruction
findings.summary: A single-center case-control study (pm_42198873, Lymphatic Research and Biology; 15 primary-lymphedema patients vs 8 controls, biopsies of affected and unaffected limbs) reported significantly REDUCED cutaneous fibrosis in primary lymphedema — the opposite of the fibrosis-dominated picture in secondary/BCRL lymphedema — alongside downregulation of CLDN5 and VEGFD and decreased TJP1 (ZO-1) in affected but not unaffected limbs. The authors interpret this as a barrier/permeability-centred pathophysiology rather than fibrotic lymphatic obstruction. Microsurgical outcomes in the same cohort were variable.
findings.clinical_implications: If replicated, this would distinguish primary from secondary lymphedema mechanistically and could reframe therapeutic targets (endothelial junction/permeability rather than anti-fibrotic). For now it is a single small study using molecular surrogates without functional correlation; it does not change management.

evolution_log.note: W24 2026 deep synthesis (new finding). Conceptually notable (primary != secondary LE histology) but n=15, single center, surrogate molecular endpoints, affected-vs-unaffected design with multiple-comparison risk. Hypothesis-generating only.

findings.title: Hypotrichosis-Lymphedema-Telangiectasia Syndrome (SOX18) Associated With Reduced von Willebrand Factor and Bleeding Diathesis
findings.summary: A case report (pm_41589511, AJMG Part A) describes a 10-year-old boy with HLTS due to a heterozygous SOX18 nonsense variant (c.481C>T, p.Gln161Ter) who had a bleeding diathesis with reduced von Willebrand factor and impaired platelet agglutination but NO VWF gene mutation, suggesting the low vWF is secondary to SOX18 dysfunction (SOX18 regulates vWF expression). vWF replacement enabled safe dental procedures.
findings.clinical_implications: Practical counseling point: consider assessing von Willebrand factor / coagulation before elective or dental procedures in patients with SOX18-related HLTS. Single-case evidence — association, not established causation.

evolution_log.note: W24 2026 deep synthesis (new finding). First reported HLTS-vWF association; mechanistically plausible (SOX18->vWF) but n=1. Flagged as practice-relevant counseling caution, not a confirmed syndromic feature.

findings.title: VEGFR3-HSPG2 (Perlecan) Interaction Required for Lymphatic Function: Novel Milroy-Relevant Mechanism (Preprint)
findings.summary: A bioRxiv preprint (ss_3c57b92f..., 2026-01-29) reports that the interaction between VEGFR3 (FLT4 — the Milroy disease gene) and the heparan-sulfate proteoglycan HSPG2/perlecan is required for normal lymphatic function in an animal model; disrupting it caused lymphatic reflux dysfunction and sepsis. Identifies HSPG2 as a novel VEGFR3 binding partner.
findings.clinical_implications: Potentially relevant to VEGFR3-dependent primary lymphedema (Milroy), but this is an unreviewed preprint in an animal model. Lymphatic biology has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record; no clinical inference is warranted.

evolution_log.note: W24 2026 deep synthesis (new finding). FLAGGED: bioRxiv preprint, not peer-reviewed; animal model only. Tracked because it touches the Milroy/VEGFR3 axis, but kept at lowest confidence pending peer review.

findings.title: Childhood-Onset Primary Lymphedema as a Presenting Sign of GATA2 Deficiency (Emberger Spectrum)
findings.summary: A case report (pm_42246350) describes a 31-year-old woman whose childhood-onset progressive primary lymphedema — with treatment-resistant warts and severe monocytopenia — led to a diagnosis of GATA2 deficiency. Reinforces that primary lymphedema can be the sentinel cutaneous sign of GATA2 deficiency (Emberger syndrome / MonoMAC), which carries risk of myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia.
findings.clinical_implications: Recognition point: unexplained primary lymphedema with cytopenia/immunodeficiency or recurrent warts should prompt consideration of GATA2 deficiency, because of its haematological malignancy risk. Single-case, but the clinical recognition message is well established.

evolution_log.note: W24 2026 deep synthesis (new finding). Adds a GATA2/Emberger recognition node to the genetics dimension.

findings.title: Italian Cohort (n=408) Identifies 18 Likely-Pathogenic Transcription-Factor-Network Variants (FOXC1/NOTCH1/RORC/FOXC2/SOX18)
findings.summary: The same 408-patient Italian primary lymphedema cohort behind the previously incorporated HGF-MET (Kozáčiková 2025) and RAS-MAPK (Belanova 2025) publications has now published a transcription-factor network analysis (Lymphology, December 2025). Screening FOXC1, NOTCH1, RORC, FOXC2, and SOX18, the authors identify 18 likely-pathogenic variants across the 5 genes, most previously unreported. FOXC2 and SOX18 are already established primary lymphedema genes (lymphedema-distichiasis and hypotrichosis-lymphedema-telangiectasia respectively); FOXC1, NOTCH1, and RORC are proposed as network-adjacent candidates based on known interactions with FOXC2/SOX18 in lymphatic development, not on independent functional validation in this paper.
findings.clinical_implications: This is systematic-panel-screening evidence, not functional validation — pathogenicity calls rest on in silico prediction and rarity, not on kinase assays, model organisms, or segregation data for most variants. As with the HGF-MET and RAS-MAPK reports from the same cohort, this should be read as one installment of an ongoing, systematic gene-discovery program in a single well-phenotyped cohort, not as 5 independent discoveries. Do not add FOXC1/NOTCH1/RORC to diagnostic gene panels on this evidence alone; FOXC2 and SOX18 remain the only genes in this set with established causal status.

evolution_log.note: W31 2026 deep synthesis: Baseline synthesis. Same Italian cohort (n=408) as finding_hgf_met_primary_le_2025 and the RAS-MAPK finding referenced in project memory — see digest-conventions memory for the full publication series from this group. Treat future papers from this cohort as continuations, not new discoveries, unless they report independent replication cohorts.

findings.title: Updated Primary Lymphedema Classification System Proposed From Largest Reported Single-Cohort Series (n=1,013)
findings.summary: A single-center series of 1,013 lower-limb primary lymphedema patients (Lymphology, June 2024) proposes an updated classification framework combining age of onset, lymphatic imaging findings (MR lymphography, ICG lymphography, lymphoscintigraphy), skin immunohistochemistry, and whole-exome sequencing. This is the largest single-cohort primary lymphedema series identified in this tracker to date.
findings.clinical_implications: Large sample size gives this descriptive value for understanding the distribution of onset ages, phenotypes, and imaging patterns in primary lymphedema, and is a useful reference point when assessing generalizability of smaller genetic/mechanistic studies elsewhere in this knowledge base. It is not an interventional or comparative study — no treatment effect or outcome comparison is being claimed, and a single-center classification proposal has not yet been externally validated or adopted as a field standard. Multi-modality imaging protocols (MRL + ICGL + LSG + WES) used are resource-intensive and may not be available outside specialist centers, limiting generalizability of any classification cut-points.

evolution_log.note: W31 2026 deep synthesis: Baseline synthesis. Confidence set to low_to_moderate on descriptive/classification grounds only (large, well-characterized single-center cohort) — this should not be read as evidence for any treatment or diagnostic-accuracy claim, which would independently need to be evaluated at a lower tier.

findings.title: Novel Homozygous GJA4 (Connexin 37) Nonsense Variant Reported in a Fetus With Increased Nuchal Fold Thickness
findings.summary: A case report (Cureus, November 2025) identifies a homozygous nonsense variant (c.97delC) in GJA4 (connexin 37), a gap-junction gene required for lymphatic valve formation, in a human fetus with increased nuchal fold thickness and abnormal ductus venosus termination. Asymptomatic parents were heterozygous carriers. Gja4 knockout mice are known to develop lymphatic dysfunction and absent venous valves, giving the variant biological plausibility, but this is the first reported human case.
findings.clinical_implications: N=1. No lymphedema phenotype is described in this report — the finding is a prenatal soft-marker (nuchal fold thickness) association, not a diagnosed lymphedema case, so its relevance to this knowledge base is upstream/mechanistic rather than directly clinical. GJA4 should not be treated as a confirmed lymphedema gene on this evidence; it is a plausible candidate pending replication in an unrelated family or a lymphedema-specific (not just nuchal-translucency) phenotype.

evolution_log.note: W31 2026 deep synthesis: Baseline synthesis. Single case, no lymphedema phenotype reported directly; candidate-gene status only.

findings.title: Gelatinous Drop-Like Corneal Amyloid Reported as a Novel Phenotype in FOXC2-Distichiasis Syndrome
findings.summary: A case report (BMC Ophthalmology, April 2026) describes a 14-year-old with FOXC2-related lymphedema-distichiasis syndrome who developed subepithelial corneal amyloid deposits histologically identical to gelatinous drop-like corneal dystrophy — a condition otherwise caused by TACSTD2 variants, an unrelated gene. This links a corneal phenotype to FOXC2 for the first time in the literature reviewed.
findings.clinical_implications: Single case; the mechanistic link between FOXC2 and corneal amyloid deposition is not established, and TACSTD2 was not reported as excluded via sequencing (dual pathology is possible). This should not change ophthalmologic screening recommendations for lymphedema-distichiasis syndrome on its own, but clinicians managing FOXC2-confirmed patients with unexplained corneal findings may want to be aware of this report.

evolution_log.note: W31 2026 deep synthesis: Baseline synthesis. Single case report; novel association, not a confirmed disease mechanism.

findings.title: Large Patient-Reported Outcomes Survey (n=10,543) Reports High Satisfaction With Pneumatic Compression — Uncontrolled Self-Report
findings.summary: A patient-reported outcomes survey of 10,543 lower-extremity lymphedema patients using pneumatic compression devices (Journal of Vascular Surgery: Venous and Lymphatic Disorders, 2026) reports high satisfaction, with daily users self-reporting the greatest benefit (swelling -58%, heaviness -34%, pain -25%). Outcomes were similar at 45 and 90 days.
findings.clinical_implications: Skepticism flags: no control arm, no objective outcome measure (all self-reported), no information on how patients were recruited or whether respondents are systematically more satisfied users (survivorship/response bias), and the described study design (large device-user survey, JVS-VL venous/lymphatic journal) is consistent with device-manufacturer-sponsored patient registry data, though sponsorship is not confirmed in the record available to this tracker — this should be verified before any promotional use. Self-reported satisfaction and self-reported symptom improvement are not equivalent to objective volume or functional outcomes, and short-term volume/symptom changes in lymphedema may reflect fluid shifts rather than durable improvement. The large N does not offset the design weaknesses; this is hypothesis-generating, not practice-changing, evidence.

evolution_log.note: W31 2026 deep synthesis: Baseline synthesis. Large N but uncontrolled, self-reported design; scored low despite sample size per evaluation-framework guidance that evidence strength reflects design, not prestige or scale.

findings.title: Retrospective Series (n=51) of Non-Image-Guided Bleomycin Sclerotherapy for Orbital-Adnexal Lymphatic Malformations
findings.summary: A single-center retrospective series (Indian Journal of Ophthalmology, May 2026) of 51 patients with orbital-adnexal lymphatic malformations (60% microcystic, ~19% macrocystic, ~28% mixed) treated with non-image-guided intralesional bleomycin, minimum 1-year follow-up. Outcomes graded by clinical lesion regression; the paper reports lesion morphology and prior treatment history as factors associated with response.
findings.clinical_implications: No control/comparator arm (e.g., vs. image-guided injection, vs. surgical excision, vs. sirolimus). Retrospective grading of clinical regression is subjective and not blinded. This adds to a body of single-arm sclerotherapy case series for lymphatic malformations; it does not establish bleomycin sclerotherapy as superior to alternative modalities (surgery, sirolimus/mTOR inhibition — see finding_mtor_mek_neonatal_lymphatic_anomalies_2026), only that it produces some degree of regression in a meaningful fraction of a reasonably sized case series.

evolution_log.note: W31 2026 deep synthesis: Baseline synthesis. Reasonably sized (n=51) single-arm retrospective series; no comparator.

findings.title: Retrospective Pediatric CDT Data From a Summer Camp Cohort — Mixed Primary/Secondary Population
findings.summary: A retrospective analysis (Lymphatic Research and Biology, August 2025) of 4 days of twice-daily complete decongestive therapy (CDT) in children aged 5-17 at a North American lymphedema summer camp (38 campers, 66 records over 4 years) reports statistically significant reductions in lower-extremity limb volume.
findings.clinical_implications: The cohort explicitly mixes primary and secondary pediatric lymphedema and does not report results stratified by etiology, so the primary-lymphedema-specific effect size cannot be isolated from this report. Small n, retrospective chart review, no control arm, and short (4-day) intervention window — consistent with the general pattern that CDT volume reductions in short programs may partly reflect fluid shifts rather than durable lymphatic improvement (chronic disease caution). Supportive of CDT's general usability in children but not a rigorous efficacy estimate for primary pediatric lymphedema specifically.

evolution_log.note: W31 2026 deep synthesis: Baseline synthesis. Mixed primary/secondary pediatric population; etiology-specific effect not isolated.

findings.title: ICG Lymphography Distinguishes Lipedema From Bilateral Lower-Limb Lymphedema in Retrospective Cohort
findings.summary: A single-center retrospective cross-sectional study (Clinical Obesity, June 2023) used indocyanine green (ICG) lymphography with MD Anderson Cancer Center ICG staging to assess whether lymphedema is present alongside lipedema in women with a clinical lipedema diagnosis, reporting that ICG imaging can help differentiate lipedema (normal/near-normal lymphatic pattern) from true bilateral lymphedema.
findings.clinical_implications: Lipedema/lymphedema differential diagnosis is clinically important because management differs; ICG lymphography is a reasonable adjunct tool per this data, but this is a single-center retrospective study without a prespecified diagnostic-accuracy design (sensitivity/specificity against a reference standard is not the primary framing here), so it should inform rather than dictate diagnostic workups. Relevance to primary (genetic) lymphedema specifically is indirect — the paper addresses lipedema vs. lymphedema broadly, not primary vs. secondary lymphedema etiology.

evolution_log.note: W31 2026 deep synthesis: Baseline synthesis. Useful diagnostic-differentiation data point; not a diagnostic-accuracy validation study.
